check: can any @GameTest silently fail to run, and does results.xml prove the full suite ran
why: The suite splits into batches - 96 in defaultBatch plus 33 across 13 named batches - and Fabric chunks defaultBatch further, since a 33-test subset reported only defaultBatch:0. A chunk that never executes would leave tests silently unrun while the run still reported success.

directEvidenceFound.declaredAtThatCommit: git show on 4e0d5e1 and counting @GameTest across src/gametest gives exactly 108
directEvidenceFound.verdict: 108 equals 108, so that run was complete rather than partial - the report file enumerates every declared test

whatThisProves: results.xml is a reliable completeness check: its testcase count tracks the declared count. Comparing the two after the pending run therefore detects a chunk that did not execute, which a simple pass message would not.
thereforeForThePendingRun: The check to apply is results.xml testcase count against 129. If a batch chunk were skipped the count would fall short and the discrepancy would surface.
methodNote: I first asserted a Fabric default batch size of about 50 without evidence, then could not find the framework class to confirm it - the server-intermediary jar turned out to hold assets rather than classes. Rather than keep guessing, the historical results.xml settled the question by measurement, which was the stronger route anyway.

namedBatchList: one each for pgw-ground-portals, pgw-tall-columns, pgw-production-memory, pgw-hydro-boundary, pgw-curved-gate-regression, pgw-survival-matrix, pgw-curve-matrix, pgw-curved-site-matrix
